The parents, which are predominantly males in this species, provide no brooding after the chicks become fully homeothermic, a transition that occurs within a few days. This rapid developmental trajectory is typical of tinamous, which produce highly precocial young capable of independent foraging shortly after the absorption of their internal yolk reserves. The incubation temperature of 36 °C is within the range documented for other members of the Tinamidae, though it sits slightly below the average reported for some congeners.

Adult Red-winged tinamous reach a maximum body length of 40.75 centimeters [Li = 40.75 centimeters], a measurement that includes the elongated tail feathers characteristic of the species and places them among the larger members of the genus Rhynchotus. This substantial gain in somatic mass occurs over the first several months of life, with the growth trajectory decelerating markedly after the onset of reproductive maturity.
